title: Loops with brakes
brief: The model must decide its own next step, call a tool, read the result and go again. Tool reliability, plan stability and the token budget are not fixed. Choose a loop shape and decide what stops it.

blocks.text: Four loop shapes and the brakes they all need

blocks.title: ReAct, plan-and-execute, reflection or a reasoning model
blocks.intro: Loops differ in where the thinking happens and what feeds the next step. Reported numbers come from the papers and are not a promise for your task.

options.name: ReAct
options.summary: Interleave a reasoning trace, an action and an observation, so each tool result updates the next thought.
pros: Simple to build and to read in a trace
On ALFWorld and WebShop it beat imitation and RL baselines by an absolute 34% and 10% success rate with one or two in-context examples [[r16]]
cons: Re-reads a growing context at every step
A bad early observation can steer the whole run
options.bestWhen: Tool results are unpredictable and the next step genuinely depends on the last one.
options.avoidWhen: The tool chain is predictable, so interleaved thinking is wasted tokens.

options.name: Plan-and-execute (Plan-and-Solve, ReWOO)
options.summary: Devise the plan first, then run the steps. ReWOO plans the tool calls up front and runs them without interleaved reasoning.
pros: Targets the missing-step errors of zero-shot chain of thought [[r38]]
ReWOO reports 5x token efficiency and 4% higher accuracy on HotpotQA [[r18]]
The plan can be shown to a reviewer first
cons: A stale plan runs against facts that changed
options.bestWhen: The tool chain is predictable and you want fewer tokens or a reviewable plan.
options.avoidWhen: Early observations often invalidate later steps.

options.name: Reflection (Reflexion, evaluator loop)
options.summary: Run, critique the outcome, store a verbal reflection and try again. Reflexion keeps reflections in an episodic buffer with no weight updates.
pros: Reports 91% pass@1 on HumanEval against 80% for the GPT-4 baseline [[r17]]
Works with an external signal such as unit tests
cons: Each retry is a full run
Self-critique without a signal tends to agree with itself
options.bestWhen: A reliable feedback signal exists: tests, a validator, a retrieval check.
options.avoidWhen: The only critic is the same model reading its own answer.

options.name: Reasoning model at higher effort
options.summary: Move part of the loop inside the model and spend reasoning tokens before acting.
pros: Fewer scripted steps in your code
Often better at planning tool use
cons: Reasoning tokens are billed as output
Latency to the first visible token rises
options.bestWhen: Evals show a quality gain that justifies the latency and cost.
options.avoidWhen: Voice, classification or retrieval steps where speed matters more.

blocks.title: Input tokens of a naive loop

vars.v: number of model calls in the run
tokens in the fixed prefix (instructions, tools, task)
tokens added to the context by each step

blocks.example: With P = 6,000, d = 1,500 and n = 20: 20 x 6,000 + 1,500 x 190 = 120,000 + 285,000 = **405,000** input tokens. The second term is quadratic, so clearing, compacting or caching it matters more than shaving the prefix. Manus reports an average input to output token ratio of about 100:1 for its agent [[r7]].

items.symptom: The same tool call with the same arguments repeats until the cap
items.cause: The tool error carries no new information, so the model retries
items.fix: Detect repeated calls, return structured errors with a hint, cap retries per tool and stop with reason repeated_call.

items.symptom: A partial draft is shown to the user as if it were complete
items.cause: The budget was hit and the harness returned the last message without a stop reason
items.fix: Return and log the stop reason, mark the answer incomplete and track the stop-reason mix as a metric.

items.symptom: Step 6 of the plan fails because step 3 changed the facts
items.fix: Re-plan on tool errors or surprising observations and cap the number of re-plans.

items.symptom: Critic scores stay flat while cost climbs
items.cause: Reflection with no external signal, so the critic agrees with the actor
items.fix: Add tests, a schema or a retrieval check as the signal, or use a different critic. Stop when the score stops improving.

items.symptom: Input tokens per step rise on every iteration
items.cause: Every tool result stays in the context for the whole run
items.fix: Clear stale tool results, cache the stable prefix and compact history. Level 4 shows how.

blocks.title: Scripting a reasoning model
blocks.md: OpenAI's guide says reasoning-capable GPT-5 models usually work best with a clear goal, strong constraints and an explicit output contract, without prescribing every intermediate step [[r34]]. Treat effort as a cost and latency dial, not only a quality dial. World 18 covers effort and test-time compute.

quiz.q: An agent loop has a 4,000-token fixed prefix and each step adds 2,000 tokens of tool output and reasoning that stay in context. Nothing is cleared or cached. How many input tokens does a 12-call run read in total? (The first call reads only the prefix.)
quiz.hint: total = n x P + d x n(n-1)/2
quiz.explain: n x P = 12 x 4,000 = 48,000. The accumulated observations add d x n(n-1)/2 = 2,000 x 66 = 132,000. The total is 180,000. A linear estimate of 12 x (4,000 + 2,000) = 72,000 badly understates it.

quiz.q: Select every brake that has to be enforced by the harness rather than left to the model's own judgement.
options: A step cap that ends the run with the stop reason max_steps
A system prompt line asking the model to stop after ten steps
A token or cost budget tracked from usage metadata
Detection of repeated identical tool calls that aborts the run
The model's own estimate of how much budget is left
quiz.explain: Limits the model could ignore, miscount or talk itself past must live in code, which is why the step cap, the metered budget and repeat detection qualify. A prompt line and the model's self-estimate are advice, so a looping or confused model can disregard them.

quiz.q: A coding agent retries a fix up to five times with a critic prompt. The trace shows the critic approving or nitpicking the same code every round while cost rises. Which change addresses the root cause?

code.code:
round 1  critic: looks good, minor naming nits   tests: not run
round 2  critic: looks good, minor naming nits   tests: not run
round 3  critic: looks good                       tests: not run
cost: 31k -> 58k -> 92k tokens

options: Use a longer critic prompt with a stricter tone and a detailed checklist of style rules
Run the test suite and feed failures back as the signal
Raise the number of rounds from five to ten
Lower the temperature of the actor
quiz.explain: The loop has no external signal, so the critic mostly agrees with the actor. Tests give a real pass or fail to loop on. A stricter prompt still reads its own work, more rounds spend more tokens on the same flat signal and temperature does not create a check.

takeaways: Pick the loop by tool predictability: ReAct for surprises, plan-first when the chain is predictable, reflection only with a real signal.
A naive loop reads the whole history again at every step, so input tokens grow quadratically.
Budget, step cap, deadline and repeat detection belong in the harness and return an explicit stop reason.
Reasoning models move part of the loop inside the model. Give goals and contracts, then measure before raising effort.
